mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances following two consecutive quarters of GDPC1 decline, or if the correlation between GDPC1 decline and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals supply chain disruptions or reduced manufacturing output, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth prospects dim.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO drops and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) growth exceeds 3% in a quarter and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by less than 2% in the same period, it signals strong economic growth without significant inflationary pressure, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 3% and CPIAUCSL growth < 2% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint condition of GDPC1 and CPIAUCSL does not correlate with positive returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 in a month, coupled with a stable or decreasing unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a strengthening labor market and robust economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 300,000 and UNRATE stable or decreases
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint condition of PAYEMS and UNRATE does not correlate with positive returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) is increasing by more than 3% annually, it signals accommodative monetary policy with rising inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns are eroded.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint condition of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL does not correlate with negative returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% over three months signals a strengthening housing market and increased consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic activity picks up.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between HOUST increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
